case_name: Lt. Col. Devender Kumar Sharma & Anr v. State Of H.P. & Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Lt. Col. Devender Kumar Sharma & Anr (husband, wife, in-laws)
parties.respondent_defendant: State of H.P. & Ors (complainant, respondent No. 2, respondent No. 3)

facts_of_case: Complainant's marriage was solemnized with proforma respondent No. 3 Mr. Winnie Sharma on 15.02.2016. She alleged that her relationship with her husband and in-laws became sour after giving birth to a female child, leading her to leave the matrimonial house. FIR sought to be quashed against petitioners and proforma respondent No. 3.

legal_principles.principle: The power under Section 482 Cr.P.C is not to be exercised in cases which involve heinous and serious offences.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Apex Court has specifically held that power under Section 482 Cr.P.C is not to be exercised in the cases which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — one reason why is that it sets a threshold for quashing criminal proceedings

legal_principles.principle: The power to compound the offences under Section 320 Cr.P.C is different from the power conferred under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Apex Court has returned the findings that power conferred under Section 482 Cr.P.C is to be distinguished from the power which lies in the Court to compound the offences under Section 320 Cr.P.C.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure — Sections 482 and 320
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — one reason why is that it highlights the distinction between two powers

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR No.23 of 2021, dated 06.12.2021, under Sections 498-A & 34 of Indian Penal Code.
